selectedOriginals.caption: East Front of Buckingham Palace
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full 2020 east-front original inspected. Three-bay end pavilions, seven-bay side ranges and three-bay projecting central pavilion produce 3:7:3:7:3 window rhythm. Rusticated ground floor has real round carriage gateways and small mezzanine lights. Tall divided sash windows, pediments on principal floor, giant Corinthian pilasters and detached central/end columns, deep entablature, three sculpted pediments/blind attics, pierced rooftop balustrade and flagstaff. Continuous first-floor balustrade and central ceremonial balcony. Pale grey/cream Portland-stone appearance with restrained weathering; no copied coats of arms or literal sculpture.

selectedOriginals.inspection: Full 2019 garden-front original inspected. Warm buff Bath stone differs from east frontage. Central curved bow has giant fluted engaged columns, large divided windows, oval blind panels, frieze relief, open upper balustrade and shallow green copper half dome; a tall blind attic rises behind. Colonnaded projecting end pavilions and low Ionic temple-form conservatory flank the main body. Own raised terrace, balustrade/urns and steps. Temporary white café canopy, people, furniture, trees and neighboring tower omitted.

additionalInspected.caption: Buckingham Palace
additionalInspected.inspection: Full 2025 east-front original inspected. Confirms the same pale stone three-pediment composition, detached columns, rusticated low storey, balcony and pierced parapet. Temporary works structure at the south end, spectators, barriers, forecourt gates and memorial do not define building geometry and are excluded from this palace-only asset.

additionalInspected.caption: Ambassadors' Court - Buckingham Palace The Ambassadors' Court inside Buckingham Palace, placed between the Queen's Gallery and the main palace itself.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full 2008 Ambassadors’ Court original inspected. Buff stone temple-portico porch with real free columns and triangular pediment, flanking lower wings with columns in antis/divided sash windows and modest roof-edge balustrade. Mature trees and parked vehicles obscure parts; only supported massing and conservatively interpreted facade bays will be authored.

sources.inspection: Owner record read: nominal front width 108m, quadrangle-inclusive depth 120m, building height 24m. Bath-stone garden elevations differ from Portland-stone east refacing. Balcony appearances date from 1851; the east refacing occurred in 1913. These are nominal controls, not a survey of each projection or flagstaff.

sources.inspection: Owner history read: Blore’s 1847–1849 east wing closed the open courtyard and introduced the balcony at Prince Albert’s suggestion. This contradicts the Qualla story claim that the balcony was first added during the 1913 refacing. Preserve the story unchanged; record the discrepancy as research evidence.

Owner architectural history read: Nash extended the central block and rebuilt the two eastern wings; Blore enclosed the courtyard. East frontage was later refaced in Portland stone; this page describes completion in 1914, while other owner/heritage records cite 1913. No false precision about construction completion dates.

Primary architectural listing read in full. Supports quadrangle form; east facade bay rhythm 3:7:3:7:3, mezzanines, rusticated archways, giant Corinthian orders, pediments and parapets. Distinguishes courtyard elevations/porticoes, garden bow and temple conservatories, Ambassadors’ Court and attached ballroom. Slate/lead roofs; warm Bath-stone west and Caen-stone courtyard contrast with east frontage. Fine sculpture and unseen engineering remain estimates.

scope: Main palace quadrangle and principal courtyards, east facade, balcony and roofline; exclude the separate Royal Mews.
limitations: Four local originals individually inspected; all 78 candidate contact views inspected. Many candidates are interiors, a Shenzhen replica, nearby landmarks, gates, vehicles or historical images and cannot control the palace exterior.

Nominal 108m frontage, 120m quadrangle depth and 24m height are primary owner controls. Native front is approximately 107.9m wide; projections, attached south blocks and conservatories extend beyond the nominal main rectangle. Preserve native outlines rather than scaling the parcel to these numbers.

Main palace quadrangle, garden bow, attached conservatory/ballroom and Ambassadors’ Court masses only. Separate Royal Mews and Riding School, forecourt gates, Victoria Memorial, gardens, neighbors, interiors, people, guards, vehicles, temporary works/canopies, banners and photographic textures are excluded.
Qualla narrative dates the balcony to the 1913 refacing; owner records place its introduction with the 1847–1849 wing and appearances from 1851. Story content is not changed by this modeling work.

Native generalized component heights of 6/12/18/21/24m are massing evidence, not surveyed storey levels. Intermediate heights, unseen facade bays, stone detailing, roof engineering and flagstaff dimensions require conservative interpretation.
The owner aerial page was located and the image opened, but browser pixel capture failed. No aerial imagery has been visually inspected for this model yet.
Independent original terrain must be acquired before authoring. No terrain fitting/flattening or footprint replacement. Ground contacts and raised terraces must be tested against the actual samples.

The native6m Ambassadors’ Court porch projection is interpreted as an open colonnade, with its solid low wall recessed behind real columns and a pitched temple roof. Original footprints remain preserved. This changes the authored mass partition, not the host terrain or map evidence.
